messages:
anya: heads-up — after the merge that went out at 11:13 UTC (PR #3821) canary perf jumped the p99 on our 8k-ish workload for seq=512. CI nightly bench shows p99 130ms -> 270ms. rolling back now but want to coordinate a quick bisect.
matt: ouch. any idea which subsystem? kernel selector, batching heuristics, or kv-cache?
anya: flamegraphs point at more time in kernel_dispatch + batching decision path. kv-cache looks a bit noisier on cold starts but not the main delta.
li: can reproduce locally. what are the exact repro steps? can run git bisect.
anya: repro steps i used (dev-box with GPU sim):
```
# checkout canary build image
./scripts/build-dev-image --tag canary-3821
# run microbench (same as CI perf job)
./tools/bench_gen.py --model redwood/atlas-7b --batch 4 --seq 512 --iters 200 --warmups 50
# summary printed at end, watch p50/p95/p99
```
li: ran it, confirmed ~2x p99 increase vs main. starting git bisect unless someone else already did.
ashley: pinging @eng-runtime — this is a potential rollout blocker for Dedicated customers.
samir: PR #3821 touched runtime/batcher/kernelselect.go right? could be a scoring change.
anya: yes, that PR refactored kernel scoring and added an early-exit fallback for older kernels. suspect interaction with recent kernel metadata tweaks.
matt: plan: identify a good commit and the bad merge commit, then bisect.
li: good known-good: 0a1b2c3 (tag: release-2026-03-05). bad: f9e8d7c (merge commit for PR #3821). starting: git bisect start f9e8d7c 0a1b2c3
li: running an automated bisect script that builds the dev image and runs the microbench. threshold: p99_ok < 160ms. script will post results here.
dev-bot: bisect-runner started by li at 1790235600, workers=4. logs: https://ci.internal/reports/bisect/1790235600
dev-bot: first test (midpoint) commit 3c4d5e6 — build+bench queued.
li: intermediate: commit 3c4d5e6 -> p99=145ms (good). bisect continuing.
anya: interesting — regression introduced after 3c4d5e6.
samir: check kernel metadata changes in that range; could cause selector to prefer slower kernels.
matt: enable ksel debug logs in the bench and capture selection decisions.
li: running with KSEL_DEBUG=1 now:
```
KSEL_DEBUG=1 ./tools/bench_gen.py --model redwood/atlas-7b --batch 4 --seq 512 --iters 200 --warmups 50 | tee /tmp/bisect-3c4d.log
```
li: log excerpt for 3c4d5e6 (good):
```
[ksel] selected kernel: matmul_opt_v3 (lat_est=3.2ms, mem=128MB)
[ksel] batch heuristics: batch_cap=4, delay_ms=6, merged=4
```
li: next bad candidate 7f6e5d4 came back p99=280ms. log excerpt:
```
[ksel] selected kernel: matmul_generic (lat_est=9.8ms, mem=192MB)
[ksel] batch heuristics: batch_cap=4, delay_ms=0, merged=1
[kvcache] cache hit rate warmup: 12% -> 60%
```
anya: selector fell back to matmul_generic and batching collapsed to single-item merges — explains p99 spike.
samir: whats in the diff around 7f6e5d4? maybe the early-exit triggers too often.
li: bisect narrowed the first bad commit to 6b7c8d9. the PR diff shows an early-exit: if kernel.lat_est increases > 2x then pick safe_kernel. That check is probably too aggressive when latency estimates noisily change.
matt: reproduce with that commit and add logging to show the threshold comparisons. if confirmed, revert early-exit or relax multiplier.
anya: prepared revert patch that disables early-exit but keeps the scoring refactor: revert-ksel-early-exit.patch
ashley: canary patch deploy? we should validate quickly and then decide roll-forward.
dev-ci: canary deploy queued with revert-ksel-early-exit at 1790235750.
li: local bench with the patch shows p99 back to ~140ms. CI nightly reports p99 135ms.
anya: recommend PR to revert the early-exit, add unit tests around ksel thresholds, and file follow-up to redesign fallback.
matt: also add a lightweight CI regression test that runs kernel selection with KSEL_DEBUG and asserts stable kernel choice across small metadata deltas.
samir: taking follow-up INF-1246 to tighten scoring and add tests.
anya: documenting triage in the incident doc and will attach logs.
ashley: rollout blocker cleared for now. :tada:
dev-bot: deploy success: revert-ksel-early-exit -> canary at 1790235899
anya: closing bisect thread. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/3987 (revert). thanks all.
